title: STRIKE– Long-Term Patient-Reported Outcomes, Functional Recovery, and Treatment Satisfaction After Conservative or Surgical Treatment of Pyogenic Spondylodiscitis
summary: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis is a bacterial infection of the spine that often causes pain, reduced mobility, and long-term health problems. This study aims to examine how different treatment strategies affect pain, function, quality of life, and patient satisfaction in the long term. Former patients will be contacted once after treatment and asked about their recovery, and these results will be linked with existing treatment data.
conditions: Pyogenic intervertebral disc infection: multiple spinal localizations

interventions.name: Patients with pyogenic spondylodiscitis treated primarily conservatively. One-time long-term follow-up assessment using standardized patient-reported outcome measures linked with routine clinical data.
Patients with pyogenic spondylodiscitis treated primarily surgically. One-time long-term follow-up assessment using standardized patient-reported outcome measures linked with routine clinical data.

Patients initially treated conservatively who underwent delayed surgery after treatment failure. One-time long-term follow-up assessment using standardized patient-reported outcome measures linked with routine clinical data

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed pyogenic spondylodiscitis (MRI-confirmed and microbiologically or clinically verified)
Documented treatment within the STRIKE-SPO cohort
Completed initial treatment
Availability of contact information for follow-up
Ability and willingness to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Non-pyogenic spondylodiscitis (e.g. tuberculous, brucellar, fungal)
Permanent inability to contact for follow-up
Severe cognitive impairment or inability to provide informed consent
